method: Nine selected cases and two repeats, each in a separate default-assistant invocation. Each generator read only the old skill snapshot and its generated task/source file, not acceptance criteria, desired answers, other cases or existing outputs. The snapshot and all forty task inputs were prepared before the canonical skill edit. One introduction invocation returned an upstream high-demand error instead of an answer; it was retried using the same frozen old skill and input after the canonical edit. No captured answer was corrected or discarded.
modelIdentifier: Not exposed by the subagent interface; no cross-model claim.
limits: A small before/after comparison with one or two responses per task is not a reliable ranking, causal effectiveness study or human-reader test.
Read-only/no-action restrictions were present in trial prompts as well as the skill, so safe behavior cannot be attributed to the skill alone.
The maintainer saw the baseline answers and acceptance criteria before finishing the revision. These are development cases, not a blinded held-out test.
The unchanged skill already performed well on most selected tasks. A stronger written method does not itself prove better model outputs.
